name: 范育成
objective:
This course is based on the management problems that students encounter at work, including operation research (OR), production planning and management, financial analysis, etc., and explores the technical principles of using machine learning, as well as the feasibility and scalability of application in these fields. The discussion scope of the machine learning will not only cover the most basic concepts and principles of convolutional neural networks (CNN),  self-attention, transformer, generative model, large language models (LLM), linear programming, and probabilistic programming, but also guide students to understand the importance of one or more of these architectures.
In terms of teaching aids, in response to the trend of the times, the programming development environment will be combined with the LLM approach to make it easier for students to quickly get started with programming languages. While looking at their own examples to achieve their own results, they will have a higher sense of accomplishment. The students also can accept the meaning of LLM’s most popular prompt engineering and parameter quantities. 
In addition, we will discuss some AI case studies, including applications of AI in medical, verbal communication, autonomous driving, education, and in multiple fields. Students will be able to apply AI technology to various fields.
This course uses a problem-based learning (PBL) approach to tackle real-
world business issues, guiding students through interdisciplinary AI projects. It
aims to teach students how to apply AI technologies such as machine learning,
image recognition, and natural language processing across various domains
like data analysis, healthcare, and smart manufacturing. Students will gain
practical skills, enhance problem-solving abilities, and develop innovative
thinking. The course prepares students to handle AI projects, understand
industry challenges, and cultivate entrepreneurial and innovative spirits.
schedule:
A. History and Origin of OR
B. Basic concepts of production planning and control
C. Financial Management and Quantitative Science
D. Differences and discussions between basic probability and statistics and Bayesian statistics
E. Models of artificial intelligence
